papers.title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
papers.abstract: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. papers.title: From Transcription to Reformulation: Defining and Benchmarking Grounded Generative Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: Speech language models have expanded automatic speech recognition (ASR) from transcription to general speech-to-text generation. Yet existing benchmarks still assume a single ground-truth transcript per utterance, an assumption that struggles when models produce readable, formatted, or structured outputs. In this work, we introduce Grounded Generative Speech Recognition (GSR), reformulating speech recognition as generating semantically grounded text instead of a single transcript. papers.title: In-Context Adapter Generation for Compositional Generalization in Large Audio Language Models
papers.abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) have achieved strong performance on standard speech and audio understanding tasks, yet their ability to systematically generalize to novel task compositions remains underexplored. Taking a meta-learning view, we extend Text-to-LoRA (T2L) to LALMs, generating instruction-conditioned LoRA adapters with a Transformer hypernetwork rather than learning a single fixed adapter shared across instructions. papers.title: Adaptive Fisher-Whitened Cross-Covariance for Low-Resource Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: Adapting multilingual speech foundation models to low-resource languages remains difficult, especially for languages that are poorly represented during pre-training. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) reduces the cost of adapting large models, conventional approaches such as LoRA rely on generic low-rank parameterizations and do not explicitly use downstream task information to define the adaptation subspace. papers.abstract: Word-level emphasis conveys meaning that text alone cannot express and is therefore essential for a practical text-to-speech (TTS) system. In this work, we study how to add emphasis control post hoc to a pretrained TTS model that has never been trained with emphasis annotations. We present EmpDPO, a simple, efficient, and effective two-stage recipe that adds emphasis control to a multilingual zero-shot diffusion TTS model through supervised fine-tuning followed by direct preference optimization (DPO). papers.title: How Architecture, Typology, and Adaptation Strategies Shape ASR for Low-Resource African Languages: A Controlled Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Despite recent advancements in ASR, identifying effective architectures, fine-tuning approaches, and data adaptation strategies for low-resource languages remains challenging. papers.abstract: Voice-interactive large language models process both what a speaker says and how they say it, yet the two channels do not always agree. papers.title: Do speech foundation models really learn words?
papers.abstract: Self-supervised speech foundation models are now used in a wide array of downstream applications, including traditional speech recognition and as the basis for tokens in speech-aware language models. Attempts to understand their usefulness have largely focused on probing their representations' ability to discriminate phonemes and words. papers.abstract: Score-based multimodal music retrieval requires representations that are both discriminative within each modality and compatible across audio recordings, sheet music images, and symbolic scores. This paper investigates the effectiveness of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for adapting pretrained music encoders and examines whether modality-specific improvements translate into better multimodal representations. papers.abstract: Few-shot voice cloning makes it cheap to produce daily Japanese financial commentary with several synthetic speakers, but kanji words with more than one reading, such as the word for "market" (shijo vs. ichiba) or "overall trend" (taisei vs. oze), are still misread. papers.abstract: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. Prior studies attribute this capability to retrieval heads, a sparse set of attention heads that transfer information from the context to the output. papers.title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple candidate trajectories, but common realizations assume that these trajectories can be executed in parallel. papers.title: Hierarchical Dual-Graph Retrieval for Long-form Audio Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large audio language models (LALMs) struggle with long-form audio reasoning, as processing entire recordings often limits to capture query-relevant content distributed across distant segments while incurring substantial computational cost. We introduce AudioHelix, a hierarchical DualGraph framework tailored for LALMs' retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. papers.title: MixCards: Evaluating Structured Descriptions of Multi-Source Sound Scenes
papers.abstract: Audio captioning benchmarks typically evaluate a single unstructured free-text description of an audio scene, providing limited insight into how a model fails to understand polyphonic audio. A plausible caption may omit a source, or conflate multiple sources into one, or assign an attribute of one source to another, and conventional captioning evaluation cannot locate these errors. papers.abstract: Speech watermarking offers proactive traceability for synthetic speech, yet most existing models operate only after text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis by adding a watermark perturbation to the generated waveform. This post-hoc design leaves watermarking as an external step that can be omitted or bypassed and restricts the watermark to a shallow waveform representation. papers.title: Speech Language Models for Full-Meeting Speaker Diarization: Capabilities and Limitations
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Speech Language Models (SpeechLMs), which integrate large language models with speech foundation models, have enabled unified sequence modeling of speech processing tasks. papers.abstract: Automatic speech recognition models suffer from catastrophic forgetting when adapted to new domains, accents, or downstream tasks. papers.abstract: In Taiwanese Hokkien automatic speech recognition (ASR), prior studies often treat tone sandhi as a major challenge under the assumption that models fail to process implicit phonological variations. papers.abstract: The quadratic scaling of attention is a fundamental bottleneck limiting the long-context capabilities of large language models (LLMs). papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks, yet it remains unclear whether their internal representations and decision criteria align with the latent structure of human cognition. In this work, we propose a novel framework to align MLLMs with the multidimensional mental representations underlying human similarity judgements. papers.abstract: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. While faithful to the underlying XAI methods, these pipelines are hard to adapt and often struggle with context-dependent follow-up questions. papers.title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
papers.abstract: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance. papers.abstract: The continuous deployment of enterprise voice systems creates a critical operational bottleneck: evaluating the acoustic quality of synthetic speech across high-volume production updates. While human Mean Opinion Score (MOS) remains the quality gold standard, it introduces severe operational costs and turn-around delays that make continuous integration infeasible. papers.abstract: We present a cascade streaming voice privacy system, consisting of ASR, NLP, and TTS modules. papers.abstract: SpecAugment is the dominant speech augmentation policy, but researchers have studied it primarily for automatic speech recognition (ASR), and it operates on spectrograms, limiting its applicability to other speech tasks and waveform models. We propose Wav2Aug, a drop-in waveform augmentation policy that randomly samples two augmentations from a calibrated pool of waveform transformations. papers.abstract: Utterance-level similarity ratings do not reveal where perceived accent differences occur in generated speech. papers.abstract: Personalized spoken agents must identify speakers before accessing user-specific memory, yet memory benchmarks typically assume correctly attributed histories. papers.abstract: Modern discrete neural audio codecs facilitate speech synthesis by replacing continuous acoustic representations with low-frame-rate discrete token sequences. papers.abstract: Abstract Aims With the rapid growth of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantations, lead management has become increasingly challenging. papers.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
papers.abstract: Evaluating human-AI co-design requires testing whether coding agents can translate real users' multimodal requests into working application revisions. We introduce Co-Design Bench, a reference-free benchmark of 273 tasks curated from 37,463 deduplicated queries across 26,314 real user coding sessions. papers.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. Building a playable game requires coordinating code, scenes, assets, animations, physics, and configurations, while allowing developers to validate their integrated behavior through interactive testing. papers.abstract: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. papers.abstract: AI research agents can propose, execute, and improve programs that solve machine learning tasks. papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of human Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) is crucial for evaluating synthetic speech quality in text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC). papers.abstract: Recognized as a top threat to AI agents, prompt injection allows instructions from untrusted data (email, documents, websites) to manipulate the agent's operation. papers.abstract: Cross-lingual dubbing aims to convert source speech into target-language speech that remains synchronized with the original video. papers.abstract: Recent advances in speech generation are shifting toward context-aware, multi-turn, and multi-speaker synthesis. papers.abstract: Neural audio codecs are increasingly used to encode speech for integration with large language models. papers.abstract: High-dimensional representations of pretrained speech foundation models have proven beneficial for objective speech quality and intelligibility prediction. papers.abstract: Test-time scaling of diffusion models with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) has become a promising strategy for sampling under user-specified rewards, such as human preference scores. papers.abstract: Low-bitrate speech coding is essential for bandwidth-constrained channels and on-device applications, but conventional residual vector quantization (RVQ)-based codecs employ a fixed number of codebooks per frame regardless of content. papers.abstract: We present a robust Speech and Audio Quality Metric (SAQM) that merges features of traditional quality metrics with a CNN trained on a large amount of data using contrastive learning methods. papers.abstract: Discrete-token-based universal speech enhancement (USE) enables strong sequence modeling but often suffers from a quality--fidelity trade-off, where perceptually plausible outputs may alter linguistic content or speaker characteristics. papers.abstract: Latency-sensitive spoken agents must know not only which tool to call, but also when they have heard enough to act. papers.abstract: Speech-based Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection holds significant promise due to its scalable and non-invasive nature. papers.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is important in human-machine interactions, enabling machines to detect and classify human emotions from solely human speech. papers.abstract: Controlling melody in audio generation normally requires training a conditional generative model on audio paired with pitch curves or MIDI notes. papers.abstract: Unified streaming speech language models aim to support speech recognition and synthesis within a single model, enabling real-time human-computer interaction. papers.abstract: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to extract a desired speaker from a mixture using auxiliary clues such as enrollment speech. papers.abstract: Although the open-source Opus audio codec is widely used for digital audio streaming, its perceptual transparency threshold for high-bitrate music compression remains insufficiently evaluated. papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) often manifests through speech impairments, facilitating accessible, non-invasive, and cost-effective severity assessment for early diagnosis and progression tracking. papers.abstract: Flow models have recently emerged as powerful generative priors for solving inverse problems. papers.abstract: Speech enhancement (SE) systems are commonly evaluated with objective metrics, with and without references, and with categorical subjective listening tests, all measuring speech quality and intelligibility. papers.abstract: Looped language models can strengthen reasoning through repeated computation with shared weights, increasing execution depth without adding independent parameters. papers.title: Does Reasoning Make Language Models Agree?
papers.abstract: Language models face two opposing concerns: monoculture, in which models err in correlated ways, and multiplicity, in which equally accurate models make conflicting decisions. The rise of reasoning models has complicated this debate: On the one hand, reasoning may increase model agreement if models anchor on the same salient features or follow similar reasoning paths. papers.abstract: Understanding how code changes affect program semantics is a core aspect of code reasoning in language models. papers.abstract: This study examines digital sovereignty in professional translation through a screening of computer-assisted translation tools and translation management systems, and a case study of migrating a translator's workstation from Windows to Linux. papers.abstract: LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4 has advanced rapidly, but provers are difficult to leverage newly contributed lemmas, because retrieval skews toward popular foundational lemmas, leaving the right premises buried among hundreds of thousands of candidates. papers.abstract: Small-scale sentiment classification often suffers from data scarcity, which limits the generalization ability of the models. papers.abstract: LLM-based simulated interviewees support interviewer training and the evaluation of mental health interviewing systems. papers.abstract: Scientific data selection is typically driven by relevance or utility scores, providing limited insight into why a document is retained. papers.abstract: Transformer-based language models have achieved remarkable success in automated short answer grading (ASAG). papers.abstract: Expert scientists excel at weighing empirical findings from multiple sources that vary in both statistical reliability and epistemic relevance. papers.title: Do Open Language Models Invent Scripture? BILAL-BENCH: Benchmarking Islamic-Source Fabrication in Bengali
papers.abstract: When a language model invents a Qur'anic verse or hadith, it gives false authority to text that readers may treat as sacred. Existing Islamic hallucination benchmarks are largely Arabic and often closed-ended, while Bengali resources mainly study general-domain hallucination or factual knowledge. We introduce BILAL-BENCH, a 240-question expert-verified benchmark for open-ended Islamic-source fabrication in Bengali. It covers Qur'anic attribution, hadith, fiqh, contemporary issues, and adversarial false-premise prompts, and uses a two-axis rubric that separates source errors from assertiveness.

papers.abstract: Human preferences change over time: an established preference may remain valid over time, become uncertain as context shifts, or be explicitly revised.
